newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes lower in thin trade.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed marginally down in thin trade against the dollar on Monday, with speculators sidelined as the exchange rate was near the central bank selling price, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 59.39 after opening at 59.36.
"There was only import covering today, with speculators on the sidelines due to the exchange rate being near the central bank top," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
The central bank pushed up the dollar by six local cents on its overseas strength, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.1947 and 59.3703.
A thin spot market saw speculators focus on forward dollars, expecting the U.S. currency to continue moving up in the near-term, dealers siad.
"Despite the demand for one-month forward dollars, the rate ended at 59.75 rupees after opening at 59.65 due to a highly liquid money market," he said.
Overnight call money rates remained at 9.5 percent, despite some active buying, dealers said.
